scenario: AITA for feeling annoyed that my boyfriend's mom kept some of my clothes meant for donation? | I believe I'm technically not in the wrong because this is all in my thoughts and I haven't vocalized this or made it evident, but I wanted to see if I'm justified in the way I feel. I kept a running donation box for 6 months in my apartment, and would periodically throw clothes in there when I felt ready to donate them. There were a lot of clothes in there near the end and they ranged from more inexpensive stuff like F21 and H&M to slightly more expensive clothes from Ann Taylor and J.Crew. Nothing extremely expensive/designer, but there were clothes in there that were barely worn or still with tags on them. I thought it'd be nice to donate everything; not to mention, I didn't have time to even think about selling them. My BF and I have been together for 5 years, and his little sister (20yo) is a similar size as me, maybe one size larger (XS vs. S). It did cross my mind that I could've given some clothes to her, but 1) I've already done that in the past with two nice coats, 2) she's never displayed a ton of appreciation for gifts, 3) their family is not hurting for $, with an income of \~$1m. His mom came over, noticed the box, and asked what it was about, so I explained that I'd been wanting to donate the clothes. She said, "Oh! I could just drop it off at the donation center in \[underserved town next to hers\], if you'd like?" I thought that was really generous of her, and took her up on the offer after double checking it was not a chore for her. Anyway, I saw his parents again weeks later and mom said, "You had some pretty decent stuff in there! I took and saved some for \[sister\]." I can't help but feel totally annoyed with this. On one hand - yes, mom was kind enough to drop it off for me. On the other hand - the clothes were meant to be donated. So.. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being unreasonable for feeling annoyed that my boyfriend's mom kept some of my clothes that I meant to donate. Let me break this down step by step. First, I had a donation box in my apartment for about six months. I was periodically adding clothes to it, ranging from more affordable brands like F21 and H&M to slightly more expensive ones like Ann Taylor and J.Crew. These weren't super high-end or designer items, but there were definitely some pieces that were barely worn or still had tags on them. I thought it would be nice to donate everything because I didn't have the time or inclination to sell them. My boyfriend and I have been together for five years, and his little sister is around 20 years old and a similar size to me, maybe one size larger. I had considered giving her some clothes in the past, and I had already given her two nice coats. However, she hasn't shown a lot of appreciation for gifts, and their family is quite well-off financially, with an income of around $1 million. So, I didn't feel the need to give her more clothes. His mom came over, noticed the donation box, and asked what it was about. I explained that I wanted to donate the clothes. She offered to drop them off at a donation center in an underserved town near hers, which I thought was really kind. I agreed to let her do that after making sure it wasn't an inconvenience for her. A few weeks later, I saw his parents again, and his mom mentioned that she had taken and saved some clothes for her daughter. This made me feel annoyed. On one hand, I appreciate that she was willing to drop off the donation for me. On the other hand, the clothes were meant to be donated, not kept for her family. I'm trying to figure out if I'm being unreasonable in feeling this way. Is it wrong to feel annoyed, or am I justified in my feelings? Let's consider different perspectives. From my perspective, the clothes were meant to be donated to people in need. I had no intention of giving them to my boyfriend's family, especially since they are financially stable. I had already given her sister some clothes in the past, and she didn't seem particularly appreciative. So, it feels like my mom-in-law overstepped by taking clothes that were intended for donation. On the other hand, maybe I'm being too sensitive. Perhaps she thought it was a good idea to save some clothes for her daughter, especially since they are similar in size. She might have thought it was a kind gesture, not realizing that I had no intention of giving them to her family. I also need to consider the relationship dynamics. My boyfriend's mom is someone I have to interact with, and I don't want to create unnecessary tension. Maybe I should just let it go, especially since she did help me with the donation. However, I can't ignore the fact that my intentions were clear. I had a specific plan for those clothes, and it wasn't to give them to her family. It's frustrating that she took it upon herself to decide what to do with them without discussing it with me first. I also wonder if there's a cultural or generational difference at play here. Maybe in her family, it's common to take things like clothes for family members without asking, whereas I come from a background where such things are discussed beforehand. Another angle to consider is the value of the clothes. While they aren't extremely expensive, they are still items that I had a sentimental attachment to or that I had spent money on. It's possible that I feel more strongly about this because of the value I associate with the clothes. I also need to think about how to communicate my feelings without causing conflict. If I bring this up with my boyfriend, he might feel caught in the middle. Alternatively, I could talk to his mom directly, but that might be uncomfortable. In the end, I'm trying to determine if my feelings are justified or if I'm overreacting. It's important to balance my own emotions with maintaining a harmonious relationship with my boyfriend's family.
